comments.text:
**Environment:**
Operating system: Windows 10
Firefox version: Firefox 127/129

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Go to https://www.kapwing.com/studio/editor
2. Observe the warning message.

**Expected Behavior:**
The page loads without any warning messages.

**Actual Behavior:**
The page gets loaded with a warning message.

**Notes:**
- Reproduces regardless of the status of ETP
- Reproduces in Firefox Nightly, Firefox Release
- Website functionalities doesn't seem to be affected
- Does not reproduce in Chrome

Created from https://github.com/webcompat/web-bugs/issues/138291

reproductions.steps:
1. Open Firefox (default configuration) and navigate to https://www.kapwing.com/studio/editor.
2. Wait for the editor to finish loading. On a fresh session (no prior visit), observe a toast notification appear in the top area of the page reading: "Warning — For the best editing experience, please consider switching to the Google Chrome Browser." with "Google Chrome Browser." linking to https://www.google.com/chrome/.
3. (If the warning does not appear because of a prior visit) In DevTools, run localStorage.removeItem('BROWSER_COOLDOWN_DATE') (or localStorage.clear()) in the page context, then reload https://www.kapwing.com/studio/editor. The warning toast reappears. This key is what gates how often the warning is shown; clearing it only resets Kapwing's own suppression timer and does not alter Firefox configuration.
4. Confirm the warning is the reported unsupported-browser warning. The toast auto-dismisses after a few seconds, so capture it promptly after load.
reproductions.summary: Reproduced in Firefox. On loading https://www.kapwing.com/studio/editor, Kapwing displays a toast notification reading "Warning — For the best editing experience, please consider switching to the Google Chrome Browser." (with a link to google.com/chrome). This is an unsupported-browser warning triggered by browser sniffing. The same page in Chrome shows no such warning (even on a fresh session with no cooldown), confirming this is Firefox-specific. Site functionality still works, but the warning degrades the Firefox experience relative to Chrome, which matches the report's "unsupported-warning" impact. Note: the warning is gated by a localStorage cooldown key (BROWSER_COOLDOWN_DATE), so it shows on the first visit / fresh session and is suppressed on immediate reloads.
